title: C634 — Exterior front door handle RH
introduction:
The right-hand exterior handle's wiring gives its sensor and keyless-entry antenna distinct jobs. I start with the connector identity, then let the cavity labels lead me into the circuit table. Think of the drawing as the seating plan and the Function column as the guest list: location and electrical role need to agree.

Use the illustrated cavity label to find the matching Cavity row, then read across for the circuit identifier, wire color, gauge, function and terminal reference. The passenger-handle wording identifies the functions covered here. The pigtail table is a separate parts lookup.

This reference supports identification and circuit-map reading. Physical access, connector viewing direction, live testing and replacement need separate service information. Gauge conventions and the Size and Used codes remain unexplained reference entries; they are not a basis here for choosing wire or setting up a test.

edits.why: The cavity labels form a vertical stack in the displayed housing. I use that arrangement to navigate the illustration and the adjacent table to associate it with the harness and shell. The drawing's page orientation alone does not identify a physical viewing side.

Each matching row brings the circuit identity, wire description, function and terminal reference together. The functions distinguish sensor power/data from the antenna connections and the remaining sensor connection. Keep the antenna's positive and negative labels attached to their stated roles; they do not supply a chassis-ground test instruction or establish the purpose of the less-specific sensor connection.

Read each pigtail entry across to its service part and engineering shell rather than treating those identifiers as interchangeable. The listed entries share a shell reference, but this page gives no selection rule between them. Their gauge entries also remain separate from the circuit-table gauge entries.
